title: Chapter LIV

teacherSummary.text: At dinner Bingley sits by Jane. Darcy is distant and seated far from Elizabeth. Jane claims she and Bingley are only friends; Elizabeth doubts it.

writingPrompts.label: Middle School
writingPrompts.text: In “Chapter LIV,” how does Austen show renewed hope? Write a paragraph that states your claim, quotes two details from the chapter, and explains how each detail supports your idea. Use the characterization you noticed as one piece of evidence.

writingPrompts.label: High School / Common Core
writingPrompts.text: Analyze how Chapter LIV develops the idea of renewed hope. Make a precise claim, support it with at least three pieces of textual evidence, and explain how the author's use of characterization and plot shapes that idea. Address one possible counterclaim.

writingPrompts.label: AP
writingPrompts.text: Write a literary argument in which you analyze how Jane Austen uses characterization in Chapter LIV to complicate the reader's understanding of renewed hope. Develop a defensible thesis, select evidence purposefully, and explain how specific choices of diction and syntax create meaning.

writingPrompts.label: College Freshman
writingPrompts.text: Situate Chapter LIV within its historical and literary context and argue how the chapter's treatment of renewed hope responds to that context. Engage with at least one secondary perspective (a critic, historian or the author's own statements), integrate quotations smoothly, and cite in MLA style.

writingPrompts.label: Graduate / PhD
writingPrompts.text: Develop an original argument that reads Chapter LIV as a hinge in the novel's larger treatment of renewed hope. Position your reading within a named critical conversation (for example formalist, historicist, psychoanalytic, feminist or postcolonial approaches), account for the textual history where relevant, and articulate the stakes of your intervention for scholarship on Pride and Prejudice.

segments.activity: Quick-write and share on the opening question.
segments.script: Good morning, readers. Before we open the book, take three minutes and write your honest answer to this: Why is Jane insisting she is indifferent? There is no wrong answer yet; we will test our ideas against the text today.

segments.activity: Model pronouncing, defining and using five key words in context.
segments.script: Today's words include partridges, detaining, enabling, venison, roasted. Watch how I figure out a word from its sentence before I check the dictionary. Here is the line: “Darcy acknowledged, that the partridges were remarkably well done; and I suppose he has two or three French cooks at least.” My guess comes from the clues around it; the dictionary says: Any one of numerous species of small gallinaceous birds of the genus Perdix and several related genera of the family….

segments.activity: Present background, then the significance of the chapter.
segments.script: Let me give you some background that the first readers of Pride and Prejudice would have known. Seating at dinner revealed intentions and status. Now, why does this chapter matter? Restraint and miscommunication delay resolution. As you listen, jot one question you want answered.

segments.activity: Read the anchor passage aloud together; annotate for Characterization, Plot, Tone / mood.
segments.script: Let's read this passage together. I will read the first sentence; you track along. Every time you spot characterization, mark it. Turn to a partner: what does the author want us to notice here? I will collect three ideas on the board and we will choose the strongest one together, using the evidence.
segments.passage: “Now,” said she, “that this first meeting is over, I feel perfectly easy. I know my own strength, and I shall never be embarrassed again by his coming. I am glad he dines here on Tuesday. It will then be publicly seen, that on both sides, we meet only as common and indifferent acquaintance.”

segments.activity: Students complete the chapter quiz, then begin the writing prompt at their assigned rigor.

Middle-school version: In “Chapter LIV,” how does Austen show renewed hope? Write a paragraph that states your claim, quotes two details from the chapter, and explains how each detail supports your idea. Use the characterization you noticed as one piece of evidence. I will circulate and conference with you.

segments.activity: One-sentence claim plus one quoted piece of evidence.
segments.script: To close: in one sentence, tell me what this chapter suggests about renewed hope, and back it with one short quotation. Hand it to me on your way out.
